CORAM: ANIL L. PANSARE AND  NIVEDITA P. MEHTA, JJ.
 DATED : 4th MARCH, 2026 JUDGMENT :
(PER : NIVEDITA P. MEHTA, J.)
1.

The petitioner has invoked jurisdiction of this Court under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India challenging the order dated 13.04.2017 passed by the Collector, Amravati,
whereby his claim for allotment of 2.00 H.R. land out of Gat No.1, Mouza Raipur, described as 'E'
Class land, has been rejected.
2.
The petitioner claims that he had joined the Army on 29.12.2008 and was discharged from service on 31.07.2013 on medical grounds.
According to the petitioner, he had submitted an application dated 29.04.2011 before the Tahsildar seeking allotment of 2.00 H.R. land out of E-Class Government land for the purpose of cultivation.
Pursuant to the said application, certain steps such as issuance of proclamation, measurement of land and obtaining no objection certificates from various authorities were undertaken.
It is the case of the petitioner that the Collector had also recommended the proposal for allotment of the said land.

By the impugned order dated 13.04.2017, the Collector rejected the request of the petitioner on the ground that the land in question forms part of Gairan land and in view of the Government Resolution dated 12.07.2011 such land cannot be allotted to any person.
Aggrieved thereby, the petitioner has filed the present petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner had made the application prior to issuance of the Government Resolution dated 12.07.2011 and therefore the said policy ought not to have been applied while deciding his claim.
It is further submitted that the land in question is E-Class Government land and not Gairan land and therefore the Collector was not justified in rejecting the request on that ground.
It is also contended that several authorities had issued no objection certificates and therefore the proposal ought to have been approved.
It is further contended that land from the same survey number has been allotted earlier to another person and therefore rejection of the petitioner's claim is discriminatory.

5. On the contrary, learned Assistant Government Pleader supports the impugned order and submits that the land in question is village common land reserved for grazing purposes and Sohan S/O Ruprao Dhandar vs State Of Maharashtra Thr. sentences.text: therefore the Collector has rightly refused to allot the same for private use.

It is 4 FJ-WP-7727-2017-.odt submitted that no person can claim allotment of Government land as a matter of right and the request of the petitioner was considered in accordance with the applicable policy.

6. Having considered the submissions and having perused the material on record, it is necessary to note that it is not in dispute that the land in question is Government land falling under 'E' Class category.

The disposal of Government land is governed by the provisions of the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code,, 1966 and the Maharashtra Land Revenue (Disposal of Government Lands) Rules,
1971.

entities.text:
Maharashtra Land Revenue (Disposal of Government Lands) Rules,
1971
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is well settled law that allotment of Government land is a matter falling within the policy domain of the State and no person can claim such allotment as a matter of right.
The mere issuance of No Objection Certificates by subordinate authorities or recommendation by the Collector does not create any vested right in favour of the petitioner.
Recommendations are always subject to final approval in accordance with Government policy.
If the policy prohibits allotment of Gairan land, no direction can be issued by this Court to compel the State to act contrary to its own policy.
7. In the present case, the petitioner had submitted an application seeking allotment of Government land and certain administrative 5 FJ-WP-7727-2017-.odt steps were undertaken thereafter.

However, the final decision regarding allotment of Government land rests with the competent authority and the same is required to be taken giving due regard to the prevailing Government policy and public interest considerations at the time of decision and not at the time of application.
8. It is pertinent to note that the State Government has issued Government Resolution dated 12.07.2011 laying down guidelines regarding use of Gairan land.

The said Resolution was issued in view of the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jagpal Singh v. State of Punjab (2011) 11 SCC 396, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court emphasized that village common lands such as grazing lands should be protected and should not be allotted for private use.

entities.text: Jagpal Singh v. State of Punjab (2011) 11 SCC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Pursuant to the said judgment,
the State Government has specifically directed that Gairan land should not be allotted to private persons, societies or associations and may be diverted only for limited public purposes.
9. The statutory position has also been reinforced by insertion of Section 22A in the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966 by the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code (Second Amendment) Act, 2017.

entities.text: Maharashtra Land Revenue Code (Second Amendment) Act, 2017
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
For the sake of brevity, the relevant provision is reproduced as under:
"22A. Prohibition on diversion of use of Gairan Land - (1) The land set apart by the Collector for free pasturage of village cattle (hereinafter referred to as "the Gairan Land") shall not be diverted, granted or leased for any other use, except in the circumstances provided in sub-sections (2) or (3), as the case may be.
(2) The Gairan land may be diverted, granted or leased for a public purpose or public project of the Central Government or the State Government or any statutory authority or any public authority or undertaking under the Central Government or the State Government (hereinafter in this section referred to as "Public Authority"), if Sohan S/O Ruprao Dhandar vs State Of Maharashtra Thr. 3

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: no other suitable piece of Government land is available for such public purpose or public project.

(3) The Gairan land may be diverted, granted or leased for a project of a project proponent, not being a Public Authority, when such Gairan land is unavoidably required for such project and such project proponent transfers to the State Government, compensatory land as provided in sub-sections (4) and (5).
(4) The compensatory land to be transferred to the State Government under sub-section (3) shall be in the same revenue village have area equal to twice the area of the Gairan land and its value shall not be less than the value of the Gairan land so allotted under sub-section (3) : Provided that, the area of 7 FJ-WP-7727-2017-.odt compensatory land shall have to be suitably increased, wherever necessary,
so as to make its value equal to the value of the Gairan land so allotted under sub-section (3).

(5)
The compensatory land to be transferred to the State Government under sub-section (3) shall,
notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, rule or orders made thereunder, be assigned by the Collector under section 22 for the use only of free pasturage of village cattle or for grass or fodder reserve.
(6) The powers of diversion, grant, lease of Gairan land under this section shall be vested in the State Government :

Provided that, notwithstanding anything contained in section 330A, the powers of the State Government under sub-section (3) shall not be delegated to any officer or other authority sub-ordinate to it.

Explanation.-- (a) For the purposes of this section, the term "public purpose" shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (30 of 2013).

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (30 of 2013)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
(b) The question whether or not such land is unavoidably required for a project under subsection (3)
shall be determined by the State Government on the advice of the Divisional Commissioner.
(7) Notwithstanding anything in sub-sections (1) to (6) or any other provision of this Act, Gram Sabhas shall be competent to 8 FJ-WP-7727-2017-.odt

preserve, safeguard and manage Gairan land in Scheduled Areas ;
Provided that, no Gairan land in the Scheduled Areas shall be diverted or disposed of without the prior informed consent of the Gram Sabhas concerned.
Explanation.-- For the purposes of sub-section (7), the term "Gram Sabha" shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in section 54-1A (b) of the Maharashtra Village Panchayats Act (III of 1959)."

As reflected above, Section 22A specifically provides that land set apart by the Collector for free pasturage of village cattle, commonly known as Gairan land, shall not be diverted, granted or leased for any other use except in the limited circumstances provided therein.

The provision further Sohan S/O Ruprao Dhandar vs State Of Maharashtra Thr. Secretary, ... on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7899606/
4 indicates that diversion of such land can ordinarily be permitted only for public purposes or public projects and that such decision lies with the State Government.

sentences.text: The Collector has taken into consideration the said Government policy and communication while rejecting the claim in the impugned order.
In that view of the matter, the decision of the Collector declining the request of the petitioner cannot be said to be arbitrary or contrary to law.
The Collector was bound to act in accordance with the policy directions issued by the State Government and the statutory framework governing Gairan land.
11. The contention of the petitioner that his application was submitted prior to issuance of Government Resolution dated 12.07.2011 also does not assist him.

It is a settled law that submission of an application does not create any vested right in favour of the applicant and the authority is required to consider such request in accordance with the policy prevailing on the date of decision.
12.
Furthermore, the plea of discrimination by the petitioner on the ground that some other person was allotted land cannot advance his case.
If any allotment has been made contrary to policy, the same cannot be relied upon to claim parity in illegality.
13. The scope of interference under Article 226 of the Constitution in matters relating to allotment of Government land is limited.
Unless the decision of the competent authority is shown to be 10 FJ-WP-7727-2017-.odt arbitrary or contrary to statutory provisions, this Court would not interfere with such administrative decisions.
In the circumstances, this Court finds that the impugned order dated 13.04.2017 does not suffer from illegality or perversity warranting interference.
14. The writ petition is dismissed.
Rule stands discharged.
No order as to costs.
(NIVEDITA P. MEHTA, J.) (ANIL L. PA  MP Deshpande Signed by: Mr. M.P. Deshpande Designation: PA To Honourable Judge Date: 07/03/2026 15:17:40
